title: Astrophysics Weekly Seminar: Ryan MacDonald – The Diversity of Worlds Revealed by the James Webb Space Telescope
desc:
Exoplanets are far more diverse than the planets in our solar system. A vast phase space of possible atmospheric conditions exists, from highly irradiated ultra-hot giant planets to frigid worlds around long dead stars. These worlds require detailed spectral investigation to uncover their secrets. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has opened new possibilities in the characterisation of exoplanet atmospheres, including first looks at temperate worlds in the habitable zone, revealing these diverse worlds in unprecedented detail.

title: SPC Seminar – Space – Dr. Niklas Grimmich (Imperial)
desc:
Title: Insights into the magnetopause: A comparison of models and observations of the dynamic boundary between the solar wind and the Earth’s magnetic field

Speaker: Dr. Niklas Grimmich (Imperial)

Abstract: The planetary magnetic field surrounds the Earth like an invisible shield. It forms a barrier to the stream of high-energy particles emanating from the Sun, known as solar wind. Similar to a river flowing around a rock, the solar wind is slowed down and diverted around the Earth’s magnetic field in what is known as the magnetosheath. The boundary between this flow region and the sphere of influence of the planetary magnetic field, called the magnetosphere, is the magnetopause. Satellite observations and simulations can be used to model the shape and location of the boundary, as well…

title: Mathematical Physics Seminar (December 2nd) – David Dean (Bordeaux) – Destruction of Van der Waals screening in driven electrolytes
desc:
Abstract: Two dielectric bodies separated by water interact through long-range Van der Waals forces, which have both quantum and thermal components. Adding an electrolyte to the water screens the long-range thermal component, substantially reducing the interaction. In this talk, I will first explain how screening arises at equilibrium through a surprising cancellation between contributions from dipole fluctuations in the dielectrics and charge and image-charge fluctuations associated with the electrolyte. I will then describe how an electric field applied parallel to the dielectric plates destroys this screening, giving rise to a long-range repulsive force, and explain this behaviour in terms of a novel mechanism involving the decoupling of charge fluctuations.
